action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

edits.description: publish: small changes Claude makes to the file at `file_path` in this same call, instead of editing the file with Edit and publishing after. Use it on a page (add `url` to update an artifact from another conversation) or on one data file of an artifact made from a type (its `url`, with that file as `file_path`). Not allowed with `type_url` or `files`. Each old_str is text copied exactly from the file as it now stands and must occur in it exactly once; new_str takes its place (empty deletes it). The edits apply in order, all or none: the file is published with them and then saved with them on disk, so it stays the source for later changes; on a miss nothing is changed or published, and the result says which edit failed and why.

old_str.description: Text copied exactly from the file; must occur once.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes the published path of a `files` entry. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` is served at its path relative to `root`, unless a `files` map entry states its served path. Claude sends it with every such publish, set to the folder that holds the Artifact's files at their served paths.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (writing people will keep editing or pass around as text, such as a memo, plan, spec, proposal or notes), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (a page to look at or use: an explainer, a diagram, anything interactive, a dashboard that shows data, anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

The user may see only the question dialog: tool results and text you wrote earlier in this turn may not be on their screen while it is open. Make each question stand on its own: if it depends on something you found, say so briefly, and name the items you are asking about in the question itself.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

content.content:
one added before `super`, one taken off in the completion before the
  caller's runs; a reopen with no URL is not counted. `isOpening(url)`
  (main only) is what `open_project`'s two main-thread steps and
  `refuseHeldPath` ask; it answers false when `.shared` is not this class,
  which is every proof probe but `agent_open_probe.swift`, which subclasses
  it (so it is not `final`). A launch whose shared controller is not this
  class logs `Frame Job: `; `agent_socket_proof.py`'s `no-controller` mutant
  removes the `install()` line and must fail Z1. A `.fjgraphic` URL never
  reaches `super`: it goes to `GraphicImportSheetController.open(packageAt:)`
  (spec §11 G-47) through
  `whenSettled`, which waits until launch and any reopening (restored
  untitled projects counted apart from #234's per-path count) are done, then
  picks the front project or opens one untitled project.
- `EditorWindow.swift` — the editor's `NSWindow` subclass: its `sendEvent`
  routes a bare Space to play/pause unless the first responder types or
  presses on it (spec §11 K-1), so Space never beeps when focus has fallen
  to the window. A new text-taking or Space-handling view must be added to
  `SpaceKey.route` and to `tools/proof/space_key_probe.swift`.
  `EditorKey.isBare` is the bare-key map's modifier rule (⇧ ⇪ always;
  `.numericPad`/`.function` on function-key scalars; never ⌘ ⌥ ⌃), read by
  `handleEditorKey` (#61).

**Timeline.**
- `TimelineView.swift` (frozen) · `TimelineLayout.swift` (every ticks ↔
  points ↔ lanes conversion; `rowTop` is a prefix sum because S/M/L drives
  real heights per track KIND) · `TimelineBar.swift` · `TimelineClipDrawing.swift`
  (a clip is ONE object: body, name strip with the kind symbol, label dot,
  motion wedges for active edges only, filmstrip under a tint wash, waveform, grips on the
  selected clip, hatched transition zone; a track paints in three passes —
  bodies, transition zones, selection rings (`drawClips`, #66) — because a
  zone lies inside the PREVIOUS clip's body) · `TimelineSessions.swift` (drag,
----
- Pitfalls, each measured: **a section factory is not a section until
  `makeSections()` calls it** — nothing type-checks the omission, and two
  phases shipped a section invisible in the app; `editedList` — a write of a
  list-valued key is built from the list it is about to REPLACE (the action's
  end list, else the base), never the evaluated one; the collapsed-state
  `UserDefaults` key records COLLAPSED, so `defaultExpanded` applies only when
  nothing is stored; a field's `refresh` is skipped while its field editor is
  attached, which it still is inside `controlTextDidEndEditing`; the pane's
  low-priority bottom pin is **249**, one below `.defaultLow`, because at 250
  it tied with a section's hugging and the solver picked per PROCESS; and
  `rebuild()` destroys every control and preserves no first responder, so a
  control a person TYPES into must live outside `structureSignature` and be
  applied to views that already exist (`MediaPane.arrange()` is the shape).
- `AssistantPane.swift` · `AssistantView.swift` · `AssistantTranscriptView.swift`
  · `AssistantComposer.swift` · `AssistantTranscript.swift` · `AssistantContextMeter.swift` — the
  Assistant tab (road map 12 A2, spec §11 AI-4). The pane builds its ONE
  `AssistantView` in `init`, never in `makeSections()` (a rebuild would take
  the composer's first responder), calls `onAssistantView` with it, and is
  exactly the visible height (`== 0` at priority 1 under the controller's
  `>=`), so the transcript scrolls itself. **The views hold no
  conversation**: the transcript is `EditorViewController.assistantTranscript`
  (`AssistantTranscript`, Rasterize's `handleEvent` ported as storage — a
  delta extends the last entry only while the previous event was the same
  delta type; `argumentSummary` drops `project`; road map 13 P2: it sums the
  `cost` events from `turn_started` to `turn_finished` into an
  `AssistantTurnCost` and ends the turn with its line as `.meta`, and
  `clear()` and `endConversation` reset the sum; road map 13 P4: every `cost`
  also adds to `conversationCost` and emits `.conversationCost`, and `clear()`
  and `endConversation` reset it and emit `.conversationCost` BEFORE their
  `.usage`, which `assistant_tab_probe`'s P1 needs last), the question the session's
  `pendingQuestion`, the session `EditorViewController.assistant`; a floating
  window later calls `attachAssistant` with the same view. **Return never
  answers**: Allow and Deny are `OptionButtonControl`s (a click, no key), Send
  is a 64 pt `AccentButton` with no key equivalent that reads Stop while busy
  or asking, and the composer's bare Return sends only while idle and beeps
  otherwise; a modified Return is a new line (spec §11 AI-17, K-2). No spinner
  (the harness settles). A label's frame is 2 pt wider
  than its text each side, and a row that holds a wrapping label is inset by 2
  pt; `snapshot_ui`'s outside_superview rule measures alignment rects since
  #140 and no longer needs the inset, which is kept. `AssistantTranscriptView`
  is a scroll view owning ONE non-editable, selectable TextKit 1 text view
  (spec §11 AI-17): each entry is a UTF-16 range of its one text (`spans`),
  one "\n" between entries, so a selection and a plain-text copy cross entries
  — its writable type is the legacy `NSStringPboardType`, because
  `writeSelection` answers false for `.string` (measured, B18); `.extended`
  inserts only the new suffix into its own entry's range; `entryLayout()`
  gives each entry's rect in the view's coordinates, and the layout dump reads
  the entries as parts it names (`UISnapshotParts`, dev only), which
  `assistant_tab_proof.py`'s `no-entry-parts` mutant empties; its
  `setFrameSize` holds the text view's minimum height at the clip view's, so a
  click below a short transcript reaches the text (`short-transcript` zeroes
  it), and `init` puts the text view's origin back at 0 after `documentView`
  (adopting it left the origin at minus its height, #182);
  `AssistantContextMeterView`
  the inline meter, `figures(_:)` (its three sentences) and `figureLadder(_:)`
  (the shorter rungs it shows, chosen in `setFrameSize`, when the full one
  does not fit; the tooltip always the full one; `full-figure-only`'s target);
  `AssistantConversationCostView` (the same file, road map 13 P4, spec §11
  P-7) the Spend row 6 pt under the meter and Clear, the rule under it:
  the first rung of `AssistantTurnCost.figureLadder` of `conversationCost`
  that fits beside its title ("≥"/"<" for "at least"/"under", still ending "·
  Frame Job's estimate", spec §11 P-8; the tooltip stays `figureTooltip`), which
  `reload(_:usage:cost:)` and `apply`'s `.conversationCost` set. Accessibility ids
  `assistant.composer|send|allow|deny|question|clear|settings|nokey|spend` and
  `assistant.entry.<kind>` are what the proofs read.
- `AssistantComposer.swift` — the Assistant tab's composer (spec §11
  AI-17). `AssistantComposerTextView` is a plain-text `NSTextView`: its
  `keyDown` is `TextEditKey.route` — a bare Return or keypad Enter is
  `onReturn`, a modified Return `insertNewline`, nothing routed while an
  input method has marked text; `insertTab` / `insertBacktab` move focus
  and never type a tab; and its undo is its OWN `UndoManager`, through a
  one-line `undoManager` override, because an editor window's manager IS
  the document's and typing would otherwise land on the project's stack.
  It also answers `undo:` and `redo:` itself (validated in
  `validateUserInterfaceItem`), because `NSWindow`'s own `undo:` reads the
  WINDOW's manager (measured, `assistant_tab_probe` P11). A set `string`
----
  straight off the call: a colour is four numbers each 0–1 and nothing on
  this side fills in an alpha or clamps a component. **There is no decoder
  for a caller's object in this file and a new door does not add one** (the
  rule under Rules; what was deleted and what it measured,
  `archive/roadmap-7.md` §2–§3).

**Shared chrome.** `Theme.swift` (`DS` tokens, including the three track
heights S/M/L per kind), `Controls.swift`, `OptionControls.swift`,
`Sheets.swift`, `EditorChrome.swift` (`BarView`), `FileDropView.swift`
(Finder drops + the first responder the bare-key map needs) — copied from
Rasterize; keep them in sync rather than forking. `Sheets.swift`'s section
under `// MARK: - Frame Job's own pieces (not in Rasterize's copy)` is
Frame Job's alone (#359): add there, and leave the copied functions' bodies
as Rasterize has them. `BrandMark.swift` is
Frame Job's own: the mark of `designs/frame-job/frame-job-icon.svg` without
its tile (spec §11 NM-11).
`Controls.swift`'s `BlockSlider` is the timeline's zoom slider. Four known
divergences, each recorded: `makeButtonRow` gives its `leading` views
compression resistance `.defaultLow`, so a footnote gives way before a button
(#141); `OptionFieldControl.finishEditing` returns first
responder to `window.contentView` (#60) where Rasterize's copy keeps
`makeFirstResponder(nil)`; every `updateTrackingAreas` in `Controls.swift` and
`OptionControls.swift` removes only the view's own areas (`area.owner ===
self`), where Rasterize's removes them all and the tooltip with them (spec §11
SH-4; kpgalligan/rasterize#335); and
`BlockSliderCell.drawBar` dims through the context's alpha rather than
`withAlphaComponent`, the one deliberate fork (SH-2) — Rasterize's spelling
paints the translucent `DS.border` track opaque in the knob's own ink.

  also adds to `conversationCost` and emits `.conversationCost`, and `clear()`
  and `endConversation` reset it and emit `.conversationCost` BEFORE their
  `.usage`, which `assistant_tab_probe`'s P1 needs last), the question the session's
  `pendingQuestion`, the session `EditorViewController.assistant`; a floating
  window later calls `attachAssistant` with the same view. **Return never
  answers**: Allow and Deny are `OptionButtonControl`s (a click, no key), Send
  is a 64 pt `AccentButton` with no key equivalent that reads Stop while busy
  or asking, and the composer's bare Return sends only while idle and beeps
  otherwise; a modified Return is a new line (spec §11 AI-17, K-2). No spinner
  (the harness settles). A label's frame is 2 pt wider
  than its text each side, and a row that holds a wrapping label is inset by 2
  pt; `snapshot_ui`'s outside_superview rule measures alignment rects since
  #140 and no longer needs the inset, which is kept. `AssistantTranscriptView`
  is a scroll view owning ONE non-editable, selectable TextKit 1 text view
  (spec §11 AI-17): each entry is a UTF-16 range of its one text (`spans`),
  one "\n" between entries, so a selection and a plain-text copy cross entries
  — its writable type is the legacy `NSStringPboardType`, because
  `writeSelection` answers false for `.string` (measured, B18); `.extended`
  inserts only the new suffix into its own entry's range; `entryLayout()`
  gives each entry's rect in the view's coordinates, and the layout dump reads
  the entries as parts it names (`UISnapshotParts`, dev only), which
  `assistant_tab_proof.py`'s `no-entry-parts` mutant empties; its
  `setFrameSize` holds the text view's minimum height at the clip view's, so a
  click below a short transcript reaches the text (`short-transcript` zeroes
  it), and `init` puts the text view's origin back at 0 after `documentView`
  (adopting it left the origin at minus its height, #182);
  `AssistantContextMeterView`
  the inline meter, `figures(_:)` (its three sentences) and `figureLadder(_:)`
  (the shorter rungs it shows, chosen in `setFrameSize`, when the full one
  does not fit; the tooltip always the full one; `full-figure-only`'s target);
  `AssistantConversationCostView` (the same file, road map 13 P4, spec §11
  P-7) the Spend row 6 pt under the meter and Clear, the rule under it:
  the first rung of `AssistantTurnCost.figureLadder` of `conversationCost`
  that fits beside its title ("≥"/"<" for "at least"/"under", still ending "·
  Frame Job's estimate", spec §11 P-8; the tooltip stays `figureTooltip`), which
  `reload(_:usage:cost:)` and `apply`'s `.conversationCost` set. Accessibility ids
  `assistant.composer|send|allow|deny|question|clear|settings|nokey|spend` and
  `assistant.entry.<kind>` are what the proofs read.
- `AssistantComposer.swift` — the Assistant tab's composer (spec §11
  AI-17). `AssistantComposerTextView` is a plain-text `NSTextView`: its
  `keyDown` is `TextEditKey.route` — a bare Return or keypad Enter is
  `onReturn`, a modified Return `insertNewline`, nothing routed while an
  input method has marked text; `insertTab` / `insertBacktab` move focus
  and never type a tab; and its undo is its OWN `UndoManager`, through a
  one-line `undoManager` override, because an editor window's manager IS
  the document's and typing would otherwise land on the project's stack.
  It also answers `undo:` and `redo:` itself (validated in
  `validateUserInterfaceItem`), because `NSWindow`'s own `undo:` reads the
  WINDOW's manager (measured, `assistant_tab_probe` P11). A set `string`
----
  straight off the call: a colour is four numbers each 0–1 and nothing on
  this side fills in an alpha or clamps a component. **There is no decoder
  for a caller's object in this file and a new door does not add one** (the
  rule under Rules; what was deleted and what it measured,
  `archive/roadmap-7.md` §2–§3).

**Shared chrome.** `Theme.swift` (`DS` tokens, including the three track
heights S/M/L per kind), `Controls.swift`, `OptionControls.swift`,
`Sheets.swift`, `EditorChrome.swift` (`BarView`), `FileDropView.swift`
(Finder drops + the first responder the bare-key map needs) — copied from
Rasterize; keep them in sync rather than forking. `Sheets.swift`'s section
under `// MARK: - Frame Job's own pieces (not in Rasterize's copy)` is
Frame Job's alone (#359): add there, and leave the copied functions' bodies
as Rasterize has them. `BrandMark.swift` is
Frame Job's own: the mark of `designs/frame-job/frame-job-icon.svg` without
its tile (spec §11 NM-11).
`Controls.swift`'s `BlockSlider` is the timeline's zoom slider. Four known
divergences, each recorded: `makeButtonRow` gives its `leading` views
compression resistance `.defaultLow`, so a footnote gives way before a button
(#141); `OptionFieldControl.finishEditing` returns first
responder to `window.contentView` (#60) where Rasterize's copy keeps
`makeFirstResponder(nil)`; every `updateTrackingAreas` in `Controls.swift` and
`OptionControls.swift` removes only the view's own areas (`area.owner ===
self`), where Rasterize's removes them all and the tooltip with them (spec §11
SH-4; kpgalligan/rasterize#335); and
`BlockSliderCell.drawBar` dims through the context's alpha rather than
`withAlphaComponent`, the one deliberate fork (SH-2) — Rasterize's spelling
paints the translucent `DS.border` track opaque in the knob's own ink.

content.content:
- **K-1 — Space is the transport's unless the first responder is typing or
  claims it** (kpgalligan/framejob#35, 2026-09-24). The editor window routes
  a bare Space key-down (⇧ and ⇪ allowed, any other modifier untouched)
  before dispatch: it toggles play/pause unless the first responder is an
  editable `NSTextView` — every field editor, the Text tab's area, the
  canvas's inline editor, the Media tab's search field, so a Space is typed
  there — an `NSButton` or `NSSegmentedControl` (they press on Space by
  AppKit's own convention, reachable only under Full Keyboard Access, and an
  accessibility user keeps it), the canvas overlay (its own Space arms a pan
  and toggles on key-up, `PreviewCanvasView.handleKeyUp`), or a sheet is
  attached. An auto-repeat of a Space the window took is swallowed. A
  non-editable field editor (a selectable label), a slider, the window
  itself and every custom inspector control are the transport's. No MCP
  mirror: playback is view state, app/CLAUDE.md's exemption, and no play
  tool exists today; `set_playhead` stays the capability.
- **K-2 — In the canvas text editor Return applies, a modified Return is a
  new line, and Esc asks before dropping a change** (kpgalligan/framejob#37,
  2026-09-24). A bare Return or keypad Enter (⇪ allowed) commits the string
  and leaves the editor — the `set_text` it always sent, one undo step,
  nothing for an unchanged string; Return with ⇧, ⌘, ⌥ or ⌃ inserts "\n",
  one rule, so ⌃Return no longer inserts AppKit's U+2028 line separator;
  while an input method holds marked text none of the three keys is routed.
  Esc leaves an unchanged edit at once; with the string changed a sheet
  asks: Cancel (Esc — back to typing, text kept), Revert (editor closed,
  clip untouched, no undo step), Apply (Return, the default — editor
  closed, the change applied, one undo step). Apply is the default because
  Return applies everywhere in the session and Apply is undoable; Revert is
  the one destructive answer and is never the default. The Text tab's
  `InspectorTextArea` keeps its form-field bargain (Return a newline,
  ⌘Return a commit in place, blur commits): it sits among fields that
  commit on blur, and a session that must be left is the canvas's alone. No
  MCP mirror: the keys are view state, `set_text` is the apply.
- **K-3 — The canvas text editor lays its text out with the renderer's
  attributes at view scale; an UPPERCASE text is edited as typed**
  (kpgalligan/framejob#117, 2026-09-30). The font, `.kern` and paragraph
  style are `LayerRenderers.textAttributes` at `video.scale × canvasScale`,
  unclamped; the font is the renderer's `CTFontCreateWithName` face, its
  fallback included. The editor keeps its own ink (`DS.textStrong` on the
  chrome backdrop) and draws no stroke: a stroke moves no glyph, and a
  clip's colours can vanish on the backdrop. `case: upper` is shown as
  typed, because the storage is what `set_text` commits and `uppercased()`
  cannot be inverted ("ß" → "SS"); so a capital wider than its letter can
  wrap where the render does not, and that is the accepted limit. A rotated
  clip is edited axis-aligned: AppKit text editing in a rotated frame fights
  the input method. The 60 × 24 pt floor still widens a box narrower than
  60 pt.
- **SH-3 — An inspector name field is the inspector's value field**
  (kpgalligan/framejob#171, 2026-09-30). `InspectorNameField` — the Graphic
  sub-tab's string rows, the Document tab's marker name and the clip
  header's name — is drawn as `OptionFieldControl` draws: an
  `NSColor.controlBackgroundColor` fill, a 1 pt `DS.border` stroke on
  `bounds.insetBy(0.5)`, `DS.controlRadius`, 7 pt padding, the line centred
  vertically, no focus ring. Its cell draws it, not a layer border, so it
  follows the appearance and a `cacheDisplay` capture holds it. The type is
  Source Sans (`DS.sans(11)`; the header's 12 semibold), not the handoff's
  Mono, because a name is a person's words. The clip header's name, which
  the handoff draws as a label, is this field at 20 pt, because the header
  is where a clip's own name is set. `DSField.style` (shared chrome, and
  Rasterize's) is unchanged.
- **CI-16 — The selected clip's obscure regions are drawn and dragged on
  the canvas; the layer's own handles outrank them, an armed modal mode's
  overlay takes every press over them, and Esc cancels any canvas drag**
  (kpgalligan/framejob#85, 2026-09-30). With exactly one clip selected,
  unlocked, outside crop mode and the text editor, each region of the list
  AT THE PLAYHEAD (the recipe's `video.obscure`) is outlined as its box's
  quad through the layer's scale, crop and rotation — an ellipse too, as its
  box — with a move grip at its centre and the eight resize handles. The
  grips exist only while the edit target's start list (CI-13) has as many

    click(view.allowButton)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""kpgalligan/framejob#35 — Space toggles play wherever nothing is typing.

    python3 tools/proof/space_key_proof.py
    python3 tools/proof/space_key_proof.py --baseline 1888069

One instrument, the probe `space_key_probe.swift`, compiled AS `main.swift`
over every file in `app/Sources` but the app's own `main.swift` on
`swift_build.py`'s line (a probe that will not build is a scored
FAILURE, never an exit). S1 asks `SpaceKey.route` row by row; S2 drives the
app's own window with synthesized Space events and reads whether play
toggled.

`--baseline <commit>` builds the same probe over `git archive <commit>
app/Sources` with `-D HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD` (S1, S2g and S2h compiled out)
and exits 0 only when EXACTLY the rows in `BASELINE_EXPECTED` fail there and
no S1, S2g or S2h row is present — the fix is what S2a and S2b measure, and
only they.

S2h (road map 12 A2) is the Assistant tab's composer. The probe runs with a
DUMMY key in a `-RCSecretFolder` of its own (so the composer shows),
`-FrameJobInspectorCollapsed NO`, and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY
popped from its environment: no person's key is read.
"""

import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import e2_chrome as e2  # noqa: E402  (the helpers: clip, project, write_package)
import reference_build  # noqa: E402
import swift_build  # noqa: E402

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", ".."))
WORK = os.path.join(HERE, "work", "space-key")
PROBE_SWIFT = os.path.join(HERE, "space_key_probe.swift")
# The item composes through the app's Metal compositor, which loads
# `default.metallib` from the directory a bare swiftc binary is in
# (`mixed_audio_probe.py`'s `build_shader`).
SHADER = os.path.join(ROOT, "app", "Resources", "Shaders", "Compositor.metal")
MOVIE = os.path.join(HERE, "media", "A.mov")
TICKS = e2.TICKS

BASELINE_EXPECTED = ["S2a", "S2b"]

RESULTS = []


def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    RESULTS.append((name, bool(ok)))
    print(f"  {'ok  ' if ok else 'FAIL'} {name}")
    if detail:
        print("       " + detail)


def packages():
    """The card of the spec, 0–6 s, and after it 6 s of `media/A.mov`
    (README "Make the test media once"). The movie is there for ONE reason:
    a shape-only plan has no media track, so `Playback.startRebuild` drops
    the item and the transport refuses — measured, `playerLayer.player`
    had no `currentItem` over the card alone. The playhead starts at 0, on
    the card."""
    os.makedirs(WORK, exist_ok=True)
    e2.CHROME = WORK
    movie = {"id": 20, "path": MOVIE, "kind": "video", "duration": 10 * TICKS,
             "width": 640, "height": 360, "fps": [30, 1], "has_video": True,
             "has_audio": False}
    tail = {
        "id": 3, "track": 1, "start": 6 * TICKS, "duration": 6 * TICKS,
        "source": {"kind": "media", "media": 20, "in": 0, "reversed": False},
        "enabled": {"video": True, "audio": True}, "speed": 1.0,
        "video": e2.video_props(), "audio": None, "text": None, "shape": None,
        "actions": [], "transition_in": None, "name": None, "label": None,
    }
    card = e2.project([e2.clip(2, 0, e2.GREY, name="Card", duration=6 * TICKS), tail],
                      media=[movie])
    return {"card": e2.write_package("space-card", card)}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The probe.


def build_shader(out, tree=ROOT):
    """The app's own `Compositor.metal` beside the binary, its entry points
    named as `tree`'s sources ask for them (`reference_build.tree_shader`)."""
    lib = os.path.join(out, "default.metallib")
    air = os.path.join(out, "Compositor.air")
    source = os.path.join(out, "Compositor.metal")
    with open(SHADER) as f:
        text = reference_build.tree_shader(tree, f.read())
    if not os.path.exists(source) or open(source).read() != text:
        with open(source, "w") as f:
            f.write(text)
    if os.path.exists(lib) and os.path.getmtime(source) < os.path.getmtime(lib):
        return lib, None
    step = subprocess.run(["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metal", "-c", source, "-o", air],
                          capture_output=True, text=True)
    if step.returncode != 0:
        return None, "xcrun metal failed: " + step.stderr.strip()[:300]
    step = subprocess.run(["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metallib", air, "-o", lib],
                          capture_output=True, text=True)
    if step.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(lib):
        return None, "xcrun metallib failed: " + step.stderr.strip()[:300]
    return lib, None


def build_probe(sources, out, reference=False):
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    entry = os.path.join(out, "main.swift")
    with open(PROBE_SWIFT) as f:
        source = f.read()
    if not os.path.exists(entry) or open(entry).read() != source:
        with open(entry, "w") as f:
            f.write(source)
    binary = os.path.join(out, "space-key-probe")
    shader, why = build_shader(out, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(sources)))
    if shader is None:
        return None, why
    swift = sorted(os.path.join(sources, n) for n in os.listdir(sources)
                   if n.endswith(".swift") and n != "main.swift")
    lib = os.path.join(ROOT, "core", "target", "release", "libframejob_core.a")
    if not os.path.exists(lib):
        return None, f"{lib} is missing — run `cd core && cargo build --release` first"
    defines = reference_build.tree_defines(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(sources)),
                                           ["HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD"] if reference else [])
    try:
        built = swift_build.build(sources=swift + [entry], output=binary, defines=defines)
    except swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed as error:
        errors = [line for line in error.diagnostics if ": error:" in line]
        return None, "swiftc failed:\n       " + "\n       ".join(
            errors[:6] or ["(no error lines)"])
    if not built.reused:
        print(f"  probe built in {built.seconds:.0f} s")
    return binary, None


def probe_checks(sources, out, paths, reference=False):
    print("\n1 — the probe: S1 the route, S2 the app's own window")
    check("media/A.mov exists (README \"Make the test media once\")", os.path.exists(MOVIE),
          MOVIE)
    binary, error = build_probe(sources, out, reference)
    check("the probe builds over app/Sources", binary is not None, error or "")
    if binary is None:
        return None
    request = os.path.join(out, "request.json")
    answer = os.path.join(out, "answer.json")
    if os.path.exists(answer):
        os.remove(answer)
    with open(request, "w") as f:
        json.dump(paths, f, indent=2)
    secrets = os.path.join(out, "secrets")
    shutil.rmtree(secrets, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(secrets)
    with open(os.path.join(secrets, "anthropic-key"), "w") as f:
        f.write("space-key-dummy-key\n")
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.pop("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", None)
    env.pop("RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY", None)
    result = subprocess.run([binary, request, answer, "-RCSecretFolder", secrets,
                             "-FrameJobInspectorCollapsed", "NO"],
                            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300, env=env)
    if result.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(answer):
        check("the probe runs", False, (result.stdout + result.stderr).strip()[-400:])
        return None
    with open(answer) as f:
        rows = json.load(f)["rows"]
    groups = ["S2a", "S2b", "S2c", "S2d", "S2e", "S2f"]
    if not reference:
        groups = ["S1", "S2g"] + groups + ["S2h"]
    check(f"the probe answers every row group ({', '.join(groups)} present)",
          all(any(r["name"].startswith(g + " ") for r in rows) for g in groups),
          f"{len(rows)} rows")
    for row in rows:
        check(row["name"], row["ok"], row["detail"])
    return rows


def baseline(commit):
    began = time.time()
    tree = os.path.join(WORK, "baseline")
    if os.path.exists(tree):
        shutil.rmtree(tree)
    os.makedirs(tree)
    archive = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, "archive", commit, "app/Sources",
                              "app/Bridging"],
                             capture_output=True)
    if archive.returncode != 0:
        print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: git archive {commit} failed: "
              f"{archive.stderr.decode(errors='replace').strip()}")
        return 1
    untar = subprocess.run(["tar", "-x", "-C", tree], input=archive.stdout,
                           capture_output=True)
    if untar.returncode != 0:
        print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: tar failed: {untar.stderr.decode(errors='replace').strip()}")
        return 1
    print(f"BASELINE {commit}: app/Sources in {os.path.relpath(tree, ROOT)}, built with "
          "-D HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD")
    rows = probe_checks(os.path.join(tree, "app", "Sources"),
                        os.path.join(tree, "out"), packages(), reference=True)
    elapsed = time.time() - began
    if rows is None:
        print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: the probe did not build or run over {commit}, "
              f"{elapsed:.0f} s")
        return 1
    failed = sorted({r["name"].split(" ")[0] for r in rows if not r["ok"]})
    absent = [r["name"] for r in rows
              if r["name"].startswith(("S1 ", "S2g ", "S2h "))]
    structural = [n for n, ok in RESULTS if not ok and not n.startswith("S")]
    if failed == sorted(BASELINE_EXPECTED) and not absent and not structural:
        print(f"BASELINE PASS: exactly {', '.join(BASELINE_EXPECTED)} FAILED on {commit} and "
              f"nothing else did, {elapsed:.0f} s")
        return 0
    print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: failed {failed} (want {BASELINE_EXPECTED}), S1/S2g/S2h rows "
          f"present {absent}, other failures {structural}, {elapsed:.0f} s")
    return 1


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) == 3 and sys.argv[1] == "--baseline":
        return baseline(sys.argv[2])
    if len(sys.argv) != 1:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    print("#35 — Space toggles play wherever nothing is typing")
    probe_checks(os.path.join(ROOT, "app", "Sources"), os.path.join(WORK, "probe"),
                 packages())
    good = sum(1 for _, ok in RESULTS if ok)
    print(f"\n{good}/{len(RESULTS)} checks passed")
    return 0 if RESULTS and good == len(RESULTS) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

SHADER = os.path.join(ROOT, "app", "Resources", "Shaders", "Compositor.metal")
MOVIE = os.path.join(HERE, "media", "A.mov")
TICKS = e2.TICKS

BASELINE_EXPECTED = ["S2a", "S2b"]

RESULTS = []


def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    RESULTS.append((name, bool(ok)))
    print(f"  {'ok  ' if ok else 'FAIL'} {name}")
    if detail:
        print("       " + detail)


def packages():
    """The card of the spec, 0–6 s, and after it 6 s of `media/A.mov`
    (README "Make the test media once"). The movie is there for ONE reason:
    a shape-only plan has no media track, so `Playback.startRebuild` drops
    the item and the transport refuses — measured, `playerLayer.player`
    had no `currentItem` over the card alone. The playhead starts at 0, on
    the card."""
    os.makedirs(WORK, exist_ok=True)
    e2.CHROME = WORK
    movie = {"id": 20, "path": MOVIE, "kind": "video", "duration": 10 * TICKS,
             "width": 640, "height": 360, "fps": [30, 1], "has_video": True,
             "has_audio": False}
    tail = {
        "id": 3, "track": 1, "start": 6 * TICKS, "duration": 6 * TICKS,
        "source": {"kind": "media", "media": 20, "in": 0, "reversed": False},
        "enabled": {"video": True, "audio": True}, "speed": 1.0,
        "video": e2.video_props(), "audio": None, "text": None, "shape": None,
        "actions": [], "transition_in": None, "name": None, "label": None,
    }
    card = e2.project([e2.clip(2, 0, e2.GREY, name="Card", duration=6 * TICKS), tail],
                      media=[movie])
    return {"card": e2.write_package("space-card", card)}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The probe.


def build_shader(out, tree=ROOT):
    """The app's own `Compositor.metal` beside the binary, its entry points
    named as `tree`'s sources ask for them (`reference_build.tree_shader`)."""
    lib = os.path.join(out, "default.metallib")
    air = os.path.join(out, "Compositor.air")
    source = os.path.join(out, "Compositor.metal")
    with open(SHADER) as f:
        text = reference_build.tree_shader(tree, f.read())
    if not os.path.exists(source) or open(source).read() != text:
        with open(source, "w") as f:
            f.write(text)
    if os.path.exists(lib) and os.path.getmtime(source) < os.path.getmtime(lib):
        return lib, None
    step = subprocess.run(["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metal", "-c", source, "-o", air],
                          capture_output=True, text=True)
    if step.returncode != 0:
        return None, "xcrun metal failed: " + step.stderr.strip()[:300]
    step = subprocess.run(["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metallib", air, "-o", lib],
                          capture_output=True, text=True)
    if step.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(lib):
        return None, "xcrun metallib failed: " + step.stderr.strip()[:300]
    return lib, None


def build_probe(sources, out, reference=False):
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    entry = os.path.join(out, "main.swift")
    with open(PROBE_SWIFT) as f:
        source = f.read()
    if not os.path.exists(entry) or open(entry).read() != source:
        with open(entry, "w") as f:
            f.write(source)
    binary = os.path.join(out, "space-key-probe")
    shader, why = build_shader(out, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(sources)))
    if shader is None:
        return None, why
    swift = sorted(os.path.join(sources, n) for n in os.listdir(sources)
                   if n.endswith(".swift") and n != "main.swift")
    lib = os.path.join(ROOT, "core", "target", "release", "libframejob_core.a")
    if not os.path.exists(lib):
        return None, f"{lib} is missing — run `cd core && cargo build --release` first"
    defines = reference_build.tree_defines(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(sources)),
                                           ["HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD"] if reference else [])
    try:
        built = swift_build.build(sources=swift + [entry], output=binary, defines=defines)
    except swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed as error:
        errors = [line for line in error.diagnostics if ": error:" in line]
        return None, "swiftc failed:\n       " + "\n       ".join(
            errors[:6] or ["(no error lines)"])
    if not built.reused:
        print(f"  probe built in {built.seconds:.0f} s")
    return binary, None


def probe_checks(sources, out, paths, reference=False):
    print("\n1 — the probe: S1 the route, S2 the app's own window")
    check("media/A.mov exists (README \"Make the test media once\")", os.path.exists(MOVIE),
          MOVIE)
    binary, error = build_probe(sources, out, reference)
    check("the probe builds over app/Sources", binary is not None, error or "")
    if binary is None:
        return None
    request = os.path.join(out, "request.json")
    answer = os.path.join(out, "answer.json")
    if os.path.exists(answer):
        os.remove(answer)
    with open(request, "w") as f:
        json.dump(paths, f, indent=2)
    secrets = os.path.join(out, "secrets")
    shutil.rmtree(secrets, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(secrets)
    with open(os.path.join(secrets, "anthropic-key"), "w") as f:
        f.write("space-key-dummy-key\n")
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.pop("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", None)
    env.pop("RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY", None)
    result = subprocess.run([binary, request, answer, "-RCSecretFolder", secrets,
                             "-FrameJobInspectorCollapsed", "NO"],
                            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300, env=env)
    if result.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(answer):
        check("the probe runs", False, (result.stdout + result.stderr).strip()[-400:])
        return None
    with open(answer) as f:
        rows = json.load(f)["rows"]
    groups = ["S2a", "S2b", "S2c", "S2d", "S2e", "S2f"]
    if not reference:
        groups = ["S1", "S2g"] + groups + ["S2h"]
    check(f"the probe answers every row group ({', '.join(groups)} present)",
          all(any(r["name"].startswith(g + " ") for r in rows) for g in groups),
          f"{len(rows)} rows")
    for row in rows:
        check(row["name"], row["ok"], row["detail"])
    return rows


def baseline(commit):
    began = time.time()
    tree = os.path.join(WORK, "baseline")
    if os.path.exists(tree):
        shutil.rmtree(tree)
    os.makedirs(tree)
    archive = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, "archive", commit, "app/Sources",
                              "app/Bridging"],
                             capture_output=True)
    if archive.returncode != 0:
        print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: git archive {commit} failed: "
              f"{archive.stderr.decode(errors='replace').strip()}")
        return 1
    untar = subprocess.run(["tar", "-x", "-C", tree], input=archive.stdout,
                           capture_output=True)
    if untar.returncode != 0:
        print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: tar failed: {untar.stderr.decode(errors='replace').strip()}")
        return 1
    print(f"BASELINE {commit}: app/Sources in {os.path.relpath(tree, ROOT)}, built with "
          "-D HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD")
    rows = probe_checks(os.path.join(tree, "app", "Sources"),
                        os.path.join(tree, "out"), packages(), reference=True)
    elapsed = time.time() - began
    if rows is None:
        print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: the probe did not build or run over {commit}, "
              f"{elapsed:.0f} s")
        return 1
    failed = sorted({r["name"].split(" ")[0] for r in rows if not r["ok"]})
    absent = [r["name"] for r in rows
              if r["name"].startswith(("S1 ", "S2g ", "S2h "))]
    structural = [n for n, ok in RESULTS if not ok and not n.startswith("S")]
    if failed == sorted(BASELINE_EXPECTED) and not absent and not structural:
        print(f"BASELINE PASS: exactly {', '.join(BASELINE_EXPECTED)} FAILED on {commit} and "
              f"nothing else did, {elapsed:.0f} s")
        return 0
    print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: failed {failed} (want {BASELINE_EXPECTED}), S1/S2g/S2h rows "
          f"present {absent}, other failures {structural}, {elapsed:.0f} s")
    return 1


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) == 3 and sys.argv[1] == "--baseline":
        return baseline(sys.argv[2])
    if len(sys.argv) != 1:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    print("#35 — Space toggles play wherever nothing is typing")
    probe_checks(os.path.join(ROOT, "app", "Sources"), os.path.join(WORK, "probe"),
                 packages())
    good = sum(1 for _, ok in RESULTS if ok)
    print(f"\n{good}/{len(RESULTS)} checks passed")
    return 0 if RESULTS and good == len(RESULTS) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

- **K-4 — Typing in the editor window is focus-averse; amends K-2 for the
  Text tab's area and AI-17 for the composer's Tab** (the owner,
  2026-10-30). Only a click or double-click — or a command that exists to
  type, View ▸ Assistant or a rename — gives text the keys, and the editor
  window takes them back BEFORE dispatch, first responder to its content
  view (the root that holds the bare-key map, #60), so Space and the
  transport keys work the moment typing ends: (1) a mouse-down inside the
  content view whose hit lies outside the text — a field editor's field,
  or the `OptionFieldControl` that frames it; a text view's scroll view; the
  text view — so a click on the timeline, which refuses first responder
  and so left the field editor attached, now ends the typing (the title
  bar is outside the content view and keeps it); (2) Tab or ⇧Tab in any
  editable text; (3) a Return or keypad Enter (⇧ ⇪ allowed) in a
  one-line field. Never while an input method has marked text, never with
  a sheet attached, and a field that refuses to resign keeps the key. Each
  field commits through its own end-of-editing path, as a blur always did;
  AppKit's own Return handling, which re-selected the field after the
  commit (so the next Space was typed into it, behind no focus ring), and
  Tab's next key view are no longer reached. The multi-line editors take
  K-2's Return: the Text tab's `InspectorTextArea` applies and leaves on a
  bare Return or keypad Enter and inserts "\n" on Return with ⇧, ⌘, ⌥ or
  ⌃ — K-2's "form-field bargain" for it is withdrawn, so ⌘Return is a new
  line where it was a commit in place — and the Assistant composer leaves
  after a Return that sends (a beep keeps it) and on Tab, where AI-17 moved
  focus to the next key view. Esc is unchanged everywhere. Sheets, Settings
  and Welcome are other windows and keep AppKit's dialog keys. No MCP
  mirror: focus is view state, app/CLAUDE.md's exemption.
- **SH-3 — An inspector name field is the inspector's value field**

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Spec §11 K-4 — typing in the editor window is focus-averse.

    python3 tools/proof/text_focus_proof.py
    python3 tools/proof/text_focus_proof.py --baseline d4537dc

One instrument, the probe `text_focus_probe.swift`, compiled AS `main.swift`
over every file in `app/Sources` but the app's own `main.swift` on
`swift_build.py`'s line (a probe that will not build is a scored FAILURE,
never an exit). F1 asks `TextFocus` row by row; F2 drives the app's own
editor window with synthesized keys and clicks and reads the first
responder, each field's commit and whether Space then plays; F3 is the
Assistant composer's Return in a window of its own.

The fixture and the shader are `space_key_proof.py`'s (the card, then 6 s of
`media/A.mov`, so the transport has an item to play), written under this
proof's own work folder.

`--baseline <commit>` builds the same probe over `git archive <commit>
app/Sources` with `-D HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD` (F1 compiled out) and exits 0
only when EXACTLY the rows in `BASELINE_EXPECTED` fail there and no F1 row is
present — the rows that measure K-4, failing on the tree before it; the
others (a click inside the field, an option field's margin, ⇧Return's new
line, a refused send) are guards that held before and must still hold.

The probe runs with a DUMMY key in a `-RCSecretFolder` of its own (so the
composer shows), `-FrameJobInspectorCollapsed NO`, and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and
RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY popped from its environment: no person's key is read.
"""

import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import reference_build  # noqa: E402
import space_key_proof as space  # noqa: E402  (the card fixture, the shader)
import swift_build  # noqa: E402

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", ".."))
WORK = os.path.join(HERE, "work", "text-focus")
PROBE_SWIFT = os.path.join(HERE, "text_focus_probe.swift")

# F2a–F2c the toolbar timecode's Return, Tab and ⇧Tab; F2d–F2e the clip
# header's name on Return and on a click on the timeline; F2g an option
# field's Tab; F2i–F2j the Text tab's area's Return and Tab; F2k the
# composer's Tab; F3a the composer after a send.
BASELINE_EXPECTED = ["F2a", "F2b", "F2c", "F2d", "F2e", "F2g", "F2i", "F2j", "F2k", "F3a"]

RESULTS = []


def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    RESULTS.append((name, bool(ok)))
    print(f"  {'ok  ' if ok else 'FAIL'} {name}")
    if detail:
        print("       " + detail)


def packages():
    space.WORK = WORK
    return space.packages()


def build_probe(sources, out, reference=False):
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    entry = os.path.join(out, "main.swift")
    with open(PROBE_SWIFT) as f:
        source = f.read()
    if not os.path.exists(entry) or open(entry).read() != source:
        with open(entry, "w") as f:
            f.write(source)
    binary = os.path.join(out, "text-focus-probe")
    shader, why = space.build_shader(out, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(sources)))
    if shader is None:
        return None, why
    swift = sorted(os.path.join(sources, n) for n in os.listdir(sources)
                   if n.endswith(".swift") and n != "main.swift")
    lib = os.path.join(ROOT, "core", "target", "release", "libframejob_core.a")
    if not os.path.exists(lib):
        return None, f"{lib} is missing — run `cd core && cargo build --release` first"
    defines = reference_build.tree_defines(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(sources)),
                                           ["HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD"] if reference else [])
    try:
        built = swift_build.build(sources=swift + [entry], output=binary, defines=defines)
    except swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed as error:
        errors = [line for line in error.diagnostics if ": error:" in line]
        return None, "swiftc failed:\n       " + "\n       ".join(
            errors[:6] or ["(no error lines)"])
    if not built.reused:
        print(f"  probe built in {built.seconds:.0f} s")
    return binary, None


def probe_checks(sources, out, paths, reference=False):
    print("\n1 — the probe: F1 the rule, F2 the app's own window, F3 the composer's Return")
    check("media/A.mov exists (README \"Make the test media once\")", os.path.exists(space.MOVIE),
          space.MOVIE)
    binary, error = build_probe(sources, out, reference)
    check("the probe builds over app/Sources", binary is not None, error or "")
    if binary is None:
        return None
    request = os.path.join(out, "request.json")
    answer = os.path.join(out, "answer.json")
    if os.path.exists(answer):
        os.remove(answer)
    with open(request, "w") as f:
        json.dump(paths, f, indent=2)
    secrets = os.path.join(out, "secrets")
    shutil.rmtree(secrets, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(secrets)
    with open(os.path.join(secrets, "anthropic-key"), "w") as f:
        f.write("text-focus-dummy-key\n")
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.pop("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", None)
    env.pop("RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY", None)
    result = subprocess.run([binary, request, answer, "-RCSecretFolder", secrets,
                             "-FrameJobInspectorCollapsed", "NO"],
                            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300, env=env)
    if result.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(answer):
        check("the probe runs", False, (result.stdout + result.stderr).strip()[-400:])
        return None
    with open(answer) as f:
        rows = json.load(f)["rows"]
    groups = ["F2a", "F2b", "F2c", "F2d", "F2e", "F2f", "F2g", "F2h", "F2i", "F2j", "F2k",
              "F3a", "F3b"]
    if not reference:
        groups = ["F1"] + groups
    check(f"the probe answers every row group ({', '.join(groups)} present)",
          all(any(r["name"].startswith(g + " ") for r in rows) for g in groups),
          f"{len(rows)} rows")
    for row in rows:
        check(row["name"], row["ok"], row["detail"])
    return rows


def baseline(commit):
    began = time.time()
    tree = os.path.join(WORK, "baseline")
    if os.path.exists(tree):
        shutil.rmtree(tree)
    os.makedirs(tree)
    archive = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, "archive", commit, "app/Sources",
                              "app/Bridging"],
                             capture_output=True)
    if archive.returncode != 0:
        print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: git archive {commit} failed: "
              f"{archive.stderr.decode(errors='replace').strip()}")
        return 1
    untar = subprocess.run(["tar", "-x", "-C", tree], input=archive.stdout,
                           capture_output=True)
    if untar.returncode != 0:
        print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: tar failed: {untar.stderr.decode(errors='replace').strip()}")
        return 1
    print(f"BASELINE {commit}: app/Sources in {os.path.relpath(tree, ROOT)}, built with "
          "-D HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD")
    rows = probe_checks(os.path.join(tree, "app", "Sources"),
                        os.path.join(tree, "out"), packages(), reference=True)
    elapsed = time.time() - began
    if rows is None:
        print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: the probe did not build or run over {commit}, "
              f"{elapsed:.0f} s")
        return 1
    failed = sorted({r["name"].split(" ")[0] for r in rows if not r["ok"]})
    absent = [r["name"] for r in rows if r["name"].startswith("F1 ")]
    structural = [n for n, ok in RESULTS if not ok and not n.startswith("F")]
    if failed == sorted(BASELINE_EXPECTED) and not absent and not structural:
        print(f"BASELINE PASS: exactly {', '.join(BASELINE_EXPECTED)} FAILED on {commit} and "
              f"nothing else did, {elapsed:.0f} s")
        return 0
    print(f"BASELINE FAILURE: failed {failed} (want {sorted(BASELINE_EXPECTED)}), F1 rows "
          f"present {absent}, other failures {structural}, {elapsed:.0f} s")
    return 1


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) == 3 and sys.argv[1] == "--baseline":
        return baseline(sys.argv[2])
    if len(sys.argv) != 1:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    print("K-4 — typing in the editor window is focus-averse")
    probe_checks(os.path.join(ROOT, "app", "Sources"), os.path.join(WORK, "probe"),
                 packages())
    good = sum(1 for _, ok in RESULTS if ok)
    print(f"\n{good}/{len(RESULTS)} checks passed")
    return 0 if RESULTS and good == len(RESULTS) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
