content.content:
The tab doesn't switch away on its own while you work in it. The assistant's own edits change the selection without moving you to the Clip tab. Clicking a clip in the timeline or on the canvas still shows the Clip tab, as it always does.

## Sending a message

Type in the field ("Ask about or edit this project…") and press Return or click **Send**. The field starts one line high and grows to five lines as you type. Past five lines it scrolls.

| Key | In the message field |
|---|---|
| Return or keypad Enter | Sends the message. While the assistant is working or waiting for an answer, it beeps instead. |
| ⇧Return, ⌘Return, ⌥Return, ⌃Return | Starts a new line |
| Tab, ⇧Tab | Moves focus to the next or previous control |
| ⌘Z, ⇧⌘Z | Undoes or redoes your typing. Typing never lands on the project's undo stack. |

The field empties once the message is sent. If the conversation cannot start (for example, the key was removed), the reason appears in red in the transcript and your text stays in the field.

While a turn runs, **Send** reads **Stop**. See [Stopping a turn](#stopping-a-turn).

----

*Agents:* `add_text_clip` (track, at, optional duration and text, either a
plain string or a text patch); `set_text` to restyle.

### The Text tab

| Section | Rows |
|---|---|
| **Content** | A multi-line text area. It applies when you click away or press ⌘Return |
| **Font** | **Family** (every font installed on the Mac, plus the faces the app ships with: Source Sans 3, Source Serif 4, Montserrat, Anton, Bebas Neue, Darker Grotesque and IBM Plex Mono), **Style** (that family's faces), **Size** 6–800 px |
| **Style** | **Color**, **Align** (L / C / R), **Vertical** (top / middle / bottom within the box), **UPPERCASE**, **Line spacing** 0.5–4× (default 1), **Tracking** −20 to 100 px (default 0) |
| **Outline** | **Outline** on/off, **Width** 0–40 px (default 2), **Color** (default black) |
| **Backdrop** | A plate behind the text: **Backdrop** on/off, **Fill** (default black at 60 %), **Padding** 0–200 px (default 12), **Radius** 0–200 px (default 8) |
----

## Keys without a menu item

These keys work in the editor window when you are not typing in a field.
They also work in the Preview Window.

### Playback and moving the playhead

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| Space | Play / pause, wherever the focus is in the window. In a text field, Space types a space. A button focused with Full Keyboard Access keeps Space to press itself |
| L | Plays forward. Press it again for 2× and then 4× |
| J | Plays in reverse. Press it again for 2× and then 4× in reverse |
| K | Pauses |
| ← / → | Moves back or forward one frame. With ⇧, ten frames |
| ↑ / ↓ | Moves to the previous or next edit point |
| Home / End | Moves to the start or end of the project |

When the preview canvas has focus, the arrow keys move the selected clips
instead ([below](#preview-canvas-gestures)).

### Editing

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `,` / `.` | Moves the selected clips one frame earlier or later. With ⇧, ten frames |
----

**Edit points** are the start and end of the timeline and the start and end
of every clip. ↑ with nothing earlier goes to the start.

J pressed while playing forwards, or L while playing backwards, switches
direction at 1×.

Space plays and pauses wherever the focus is, except while you type in a
text field or when a focused button uses the key itself. On the preview
canvas a quick Space press still plays or pauses (when you let go), while
holding Space and dragging pans the canvas instead. Holding Space down
doesn't toggle playback over and over. Letter keys never
fire while you are typing in a field, and no editor key works while a sheet
is open.

----
- **Expect:** the turn ends with `Cost: at least $… (a response was cut short) · Frame Job's estimate at LiteLLM prices (…)`; the ledger's last line carries `"partial": true`; the Console's charge for that request is at least that figure, and expect it above: the streamed output is not counted (spec §11 P-8).
- **Source:** issue batch B15 (#162); spec §11 P-8.

**AS-7 — Selecting the conversation, and a message of several lines**
- **Do:** In light, then dark, after a turn with a tool call: 1. Drag from inside a reply down into the next person line and a tool line; ⌘C; paste into TextEdit. 2. In the composer type a line, ⇧Return, another, ⌥Return, a third, and keep adding lines past five. 3. Press Return. 4. With an input method that composes (Japanese, say), start a word so it is underlined and press Return. 5. Send something long and, while it is working, type in the composer and press Return.
- **Expect:** 1. the drag selects across entries, and the paste is plain text (no fonts or colours), each entry starting on its own line. 2. each modified Return starts a new line; the field grows a line at a time up to five, then holds its height and scrolls. 3. the whole message is sent, lines intact, and the field is one line again. 4. Return commits the word and sends nothing. 5. Return beeps and the text stays.
- **Source:** issue batch B18 (#153, #154); spec §11 AI-17 and K-2.

**AS-8 — The tab at its narrowest**
- **Do:** With a real key, after a turn: 1. Drag the inspector to its narrowest and back, watching the Context figures, and hover them. 2. In a short conversation, click below the last entry, then drag from there up into it. 3. Type a message that wraps to two lines at the narrowest width, and drag the inspector slowly wider and narrower. 4. Empty the composer at the narrowest width.
- **Expect:** 1. The figures are full when there is room, and shorter ("N / L · P%", then "P%") as the inspector narrows. They are never cut off with "…", and the tooltip reads the full figure. 2. The click clears the selection, and the drag selects up from the end. 3. The field follows the width, two lines while the message wraps and one line when it does not, with no jump or flicker. 4. The placeholder sits on one line.
- **Expect:** a crosshair; the band shows its rectangle ghosted; ⇧ switches to fill; each release adds one action; every listed way ends the mode; ⇧Z still fits the timeline; Place on Canvas greys out at four; the face is really hidden.
- **Source:** #48.

**TL-10 — Marquee, context menu and Space**
- **Do:** 1. Drag a marquee starting below the last lane with a real mouse. 2. ⌃-click a track header and a lane. 3. Commit an inspector number with Return, then press Space. 4. Turn on Full Keyboard Access, Tab to a button, press Space.
- **Expect:** the band draws and the selection block counts up; ⌃-click pops the menu at the pointer (no drag starts) and its checkmarks read; Space plays with no beep; with Full Keyboard Access, Space presses the button instead.
- **Source:** #48 (#35).

- **Source:** #48.

**TL-13 — Bare keys after a field, and with Caps Lock**
- **Do:** 1. Change an inspector number, press Return, then press I, O, ←, →, ↑, ↓, Home, End without clicking. 2. Click into another number field, press Esc, then L and K. 3. Turn Caps Lock on and repeat 1 and J / K / L.
- **Expect:** every key acts with no beep and no click first.
- **Source:** #60, #61.

**TL-14 — Obscure regions on the canvas**
- **Do:** 1. On a rotated, scaled clip with two obscure regions, select the clip and drag a region's centre, a corner and an edge. 2. ⌥-drag an edge. 3. Press Esc mid-drag of a region, then mid-drag of the clip itself. 4. ⌘Z each drag. 5. Repeat 1 with an action selected. 6. Press Place on Canvas.
- **Expect:** the dashed outlines sit on the hidden areas and turn with the clip; the cursors change over the grips; a drag has no jump or lag; each Esc puts the drag back with no step (Edit ▸ Undo names the step before it); each drag is one "Move Region" or "Resize Region" step; with an action selected the region animates to where it was dragged; the outlines stay drawn under the band.
- **Source:** #85.

**TL-15 — Pane sizes remembered from a drag only**
- **Do:** 1. Drag the divider above the timeline to make the timeline clearly taller, and the divider beside the inspector to make it wider. 2. Open a new window (File ▸ New). 3. In that window, make the window itself much smaller and then larger again, and press ⌥⌘I twice. 4. Open a third window.
- **Expect:** the second window opens with the timeline height and inspector width from step 1; the third opens with those same sizes, not the ones the window resize in step 3 left behind.
- **Source:** #327.

## Clip tab and action lane

Run each in both appearances. An action is a keyframed segment (Clip ▸ Add Action, ⌥⌘K).

# Manual checks

The standing list of checks only a person at the machine can do: things
that need eyes, ears, a real mouse and keyboard, a second display, a real
network, a real API key or macOS permissions. Everything a script can
measure is already in `tools/proof/` and is not repeated here.

**When to run it.** Run every section before a release. Between releases,
run the sections whose area changed. Unless a check says otherwise, run it
in both appearances (System Settings ▸ Appearance, Light then Dark).

## Setup, once per run

1. Build: `make app`.
2. Open the Release app from the Finder, or with
   `open "build/Build/Products/Release/Frame Job.app"`. **Not from a terminal**:
   a terminal-launched app's permissions (Screen Recording, Microphone)
   belong to the terminal, not to Frame Job. Only REC-3, REC-7, REC-8's

## Space is the transport's (`space_key_proof.py`, `space_key_probe.swift`)

kpgalligan/framejob#35, spec §11 K-1: a bare Space toggles play from any
focus but a field being typed into, decided by `EditorWindow.sendEvent`
before dispatch. The probe is compiled AS `main.swift` over `app/Sources`
(`harness/build.sh`'s swiftc line, a build failure is a scored FAILURE) with
the app's `Compositor.metal` built into a `default.metallib` beside it. S1
asks `SpaceKey.route` directly — window, plain view and slider are the
transport's; an editable `NSTextView`, `NSButton`, `NSPopUpButton`,
`NSSegmentedControl`, `CanvasOverlayView` and an attached sheet keep the
key; an auto-repeat is held; ⌘/⌥/⌃ Space, a `j` and a key-up are not
routed; ⇧ and ⇪ are. S2 drives the app's OWN window
(`makeWindowControllers()`) with synthesized events through
`NSWindow.sendEvent` and reads `editor.playback.isPlaying`: (a) from the
window as first responder — the state an inspector field's commit leaves —
Space plays and pauses; (b) a custom view first responder never sees the
key and play toggles; (c) the timecode field types it; (d) the canvas
overlay toggles on key-UP; (e) an `NSButton` first responder is handed the
Space (its `keyDown` sees it once — whether AppKit then presses it depends on
Full Keyboard Access, a host setting, so FKA and the press are printed in the
detail and not scored; #48 is the press's
hands-on check); (f) an auto-repeat is
swallowed; (g) the window is an `EditorWindow`; (h) (road map 12 A2) the
Assistant tab's composer, shown by `showAssistant` — View ▸ Assistant's own
method — and first responder, types the Space and play stays paused. For (h)
the probe runs with a DUMMY key in a `-RCSecretFolder` of its own (so the
composer shows), `-FrameJobInspectorCollapsed NO`, and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and
`RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` popped from its environment. The beep is not observable;
(a) and (b) together are the claim that the window returned before
`super.sendEvent`.

The package is the grey card at 0–6 s plus 6 s of `media/A.mov` after it:
over a shape-only plan `Playback` has no item and `play()` refuses, so a
media track is what lets the transport move. Needs `media/A.mov` (a scored
row when missing), no ffmpeg.

app/Sources` with `-D HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD` (S1, S2g and S2h compiled out)
in `work/space-key/baseline/`, and exits 0 only when EXACTLY S2a and S2b fail
there and no S1, S2g or S2h row is present. Measured 2026-09-24: 28/28 on the
fix; `--baseline 1888069` fails exactly S2a and S2b and exits 0. Measured
2026-09-27 with S2h (road map 12 A2): 29/29, and the baseline still exactly
S2a and S2b. Road map 2 §2 Phase 8's #35 record says why
S2e scores the hand-off rather than the press.

## Typing gives the keys back (`text_focus_proof.py`, `text_focus_probe.swift`)

Spec §11 K-4: typing in the editor window is focus-averse —
`EditorWindow.sendEvent` asks `TextFocus` before dispatch, and a click
outside the text, Tab (Full Keyboard Access off) or a Return in a one-line
field hands first responder to the content view. Built and run as
`space_key_proof.py`'s probe is, over the same card package (written under
`work/text-focus/`) and with the same dummy key and environment. F1 asks
`TextFocus` directly: which responder is typing; Return, keypad Enter, ⇧ and
⇪ Return leave a field editor and ⌥/⌘/⌃ Return do not; Tab and ⇧Tab leave
any text unless Full Keyboard Access is on, ⌃Tab and ⌥Tab never; marked
text keeps every key; a click's host is the field (or the
`OptionFieldControl` framing it), else the scroll view, else the text view,
and a hit outside the content view (nil) never leaves. F2 drives the app's
OWN window with synthesized keys and mouse-downs (each mouse-up queued
first, so a field editor's tracking loop ends) and reads the first
responder, the commit and whether Space then plays: (z) the host's Full
Keyboard Access is off, the Tab rows' premise; (a–c) the toolbar timecode's
Return, Tab and ⇧Tab; (d) the clip header's name on Return; (e) the same
name on a click on the timeline; (f) a click inside the field keeps it;
(g–h) an `OptionFieldControl`'s Tab, and a click on its own margin keeping
it; (i–j) the Text tab's area — ⇧Return a new line, Return applies once,
Tab applies; (k) the composer's Tab after View ▸ Assistant. F3 is the
composer's Return in a window of its own: a send leaves, a refused send
keeps the text and the keys.

`--baseline <commit>` builds the probe over that commit's `app/Sources`
with `-D HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD` (F1 compiled out) and exits 0 only when
EXACTLY `BASELINE_EXPECTED` fails. Measured 2026-10-30: 57/57 on the fix;
`--baseline d4537dc` fails exactly F2b, F2d, F2e, F2g, F2i, F2j, F2k and F3a
(F2d: the name committed, then its field editor was first responder again
and Space was typed into it; F2e: the timeline click committed nothing).
F2a and F2c held there — the toolbar timecode's delegate already handed
the keys back — and are guards. Eight mutants, each killed: the click
branch, the field editor's Return, the `OptionFieldControl` host, marked
text, Full Keyboard Access, the scroll-view host, the composer's send and
the area's Return.

```sh
python3 tools/proof/text_focus_proof.py                     # → 57/57
python3 tools/proof/text_focus_proof.py --baseline d4537dc  # exit 0 = exactly the eight FAIL
```

content.text:
Text fields in the editor window now let go of the keys. After Return, Tab or a click anywhere outside the field, the value is applied and Space plays straight away. The gate and the proofs all pass; nothing is committed.

**What was wrong.** Two things, both hidden because these fields draw no focus ring:
- **Return:** the value was saved, then AppKit put the cursor straight back in the field with its text selected. That's the "re-focus" you saw: the next Space replaced the text.
- **Clicking the timeline:** the timeline never takes the keyboard, so the field quietly kept it, with nothing saved.

**The fix.** One rule in `app/Sources/EditorWindow.swift`, checked before each key or click reaches anything else. It covers every text field in the window (inspector fields, the toolbar timecode, the Media search, timeline renames, the canvas text editor, the Assistant message field), and new fields get it without extra code:
- A click outside the field you're typing in ends the typing. The title bar is excluded.
- Tab ends it in any field. Return ends it in one-line fields.
- Each field saves through its normal path, once, as it does when it loses focus.

**Behaviour changes to check:**
- **Text tab's Content area:** Return now applies the text and lets go, and ⇧Return starts a new line, matching the canvas text editor. ⌘Return is now a new line; it used to apply the text and stay in the field. This reverses part of an earlier recorded decision, so I wrote it up as a new one (K-4 in `designs/spec/11-decisions/chrome-inspector-keys.md`).
- **Assistant message field:** after Return sends, the keys go back to the editor, so Space plays while the assistant works. If Return only beeps because it's busy, the field keeps them.
- **Full Keyboard Access:** I kept Tab moving between controls when it's on. Otherwise a keyboard-only user could never get past the first text field. Return and click-away still let go. This is the same exception the Space rule already makes for buttons.
- Esc is unchanged. Sheets, Settings and the Welcome window are separate windows and keep the normal dialog keys.

**Verification:**
- **New proof:** `tools/proof/text_focus_proof.py` drives the app's real editor window with simulated keys and clicks and passes 57/57.
- **Bug reproduced:** run on the code before the fix, it fails exactly the 8 rows that show your bug. In one, Return saved the clip's name and the field took the keys straight back, so Space was typed into it.
- **Mutants:** I broke each decision in the change one at a time (8 in all), and the proof caught every one.
- **Other proofs:** `make gate` passes; the Space-key proof passes 29/29 and the Assistant tab proof 26/26 against the Release app.

**For you to try:** a simulated event isn't a real keyboard and mouse, so I added a check to `docs/manual-checks.md` (TL-16) covering the steps you described. I also updated the user guide pages and the proofs README.

content.text:
One-line text fields in the inspector now stretch to the full width of the row; they were capped at 170 pt. The gate passes and the graphics inspector proof passes 100/100 against the Release app. Nothing is committed yet.

- **What stretches:** a graphic's one-line string properties (your kicker/title/chips) and the Document tab's marker name. At the default 304 pt inspector the field grows from 170 to 188 pt; at the widest (440 pt) it's 324 pt.
- **Long text** scrolls inside the field instead of widening the row.
- **With an action selected,** a row that switches at the action's end still shows its "at end" tag; the field shrinks to make room for it.
- **The fix** is one rule in `inspectorRow` (`app/Sources/InspectorRows.swift`), so any future one-line field in an inspector row stretches the same way.

**Multi-line already exists.** Add `multiline: true` to a string property in the module's schema and its row becomes a full-width text area:

```js
items: { type: "string", default: "Intro\nDemo\nQuestions", multiline: true }
```

It's documented in `docs/graphics-api.md` with that example, and the bundled Quote card uses it for its quote. After today's earlier change, Return applies the text and ⇧Return starts a new line. Your "chips" property isn't from a bundled template, so whether it becomes one-per-line is up to that module. Its render code would have to split on new lines instead of commas.

**Recorded and checked:**
- The 170 pt cap was a recorded decision (G-34), so I recorded the change as G-48 in `designs/spec/11-decisions/graphics.md`.
- The proof row that pinned 170 pt now checks the new rule at both 304 and 440 pt. It confirms the field fills the row, and that when keyed it ends before a whole "at end" tag and gives way to it.
- The mutant tied to the old width was replaced with two new ones, and both are caught. The second survived at first: without the field's lower priority, the field and the tag tie, and Auto Layout happened to shrink the field. A tie can settle differently in another run, so the row now also checks that the field gives way first.
- The graphics guide and the Swift file notes (`app/CLAUDE.md`) are updated.
